bull.b: The high recurring-revenue mix supports predictable sales visibility and customer lifetime value. Usage-based SaaS subscriptions can expand as customers add data, users, channels and messaging volume, creating a durable base for growth.

Strong current growth, sizeable remaining performance obligations and continued double-digit guidance indicate sustained enterprise demand. Contracted backlog improves revenue visibility while product adoption and larger deals support multi-period expansion.

bull.t: Retention, enterprise expansion and cash generation
bull.b: Net retention above 100% shows existing customers are expanding spend, while enterprise growth strengthens account quality. Positive and improving free cash flow adds internal funding capacity and reduces reliance on external capital as Braze scales.

bear.b: Braze has improved losses but still lacks sustainable GAAP earnings power. Continued losses can erode equity and limit the durability of reported progress, especially if growth investments remain elevated or revenue expansion slows further.

Premium messaging and carrier costs can rise with customer channel mix, while AI product delivery requires additional personnel. Even when fees are passed through, persistent mix and service-cost pressure may constrain long-term margin expansion.

Braze must integrate rapid headcount growth and expand delivery capacity while managing a CFO transition. Execution missteps could delay product deployments, increase operating costs or weaken financial discipline during an important scaling phase.
